This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and moneylines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 4. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills (-6.5, 48.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, New York Josh Allen and the Bills split their series with the Patriots last season. Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire The Buffalo Bills , the AFC favorite to reach the Super Bowl, will host last season's AFC Super Bowl representative, the New England Patriots , in a matchup of AFC East rivals Sunday. The Patriots will need game plan answers on both sides of the ball to counter the Bills' high-scoring offense, and they'll have to create a more defined passing game without A.J. Brown (ankle) on the field. I like the Bills to win and cover in this one, and in a divisional game with this level of coaching and familiarity, I'll take the under on the total. Let's check out both clubs, and I'll add some props at the end to play, too. It happens in this league. But don't let one game change the narrative on an explosive Bills offense leading the NFL in scoring (33.7 PPG) and producing top-10 numbers in both passing and rushing. Quarterback Josh Allen will see heavy single-high coverage from New England (both man and zone), which creates opportunities for the Bills to scheme for crossing concepts and big-play throws on deep over routes, and they can also attack the seams with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The man matchup to watch to here is DJ Moore against Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), if the Patriots corner is up for the game. Best versus best. And let's not forget the offensive balance the Bills have with running back James Cook III , who has produced back-to-back games with at least 135 yards rushing, against a New England defense allowing 4.8 YPC. The question I always have for teams versus Allen, given his dual-threat ability, is how much man coverage can you play? And what is your answer for Allen as a runner in the low red zone? Let's see how the Patriots counter, as Allen has rushed for two scores in all three games played this season. He's the league's ultimate difference-maker. When the Patriots have the ball: Quarterback Drake Maye has made some reckless decisions with the ball, throwing a league-high six interceptions and registering a 45.9 QBR (25th in the league). But I'm not going to put this all on Maye, as the Patriots' wide receiver group is lacking juice and matchup edges. With Brown on IR, who is the boundary X to win the one-on-ones? The tape shows us that the New England wideouts aren't creating separation at a high rate. The key here is for Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to scheme more defined throws -- while having answers to pressure -- versus a Bills defense that has been more zone-heavy (65.9% of opponent dropbacks). Maye is going to see split-safety coverage. Lift the safeties here and create those middle-of-the-field voids for the quarterback to drive the ball. More importantly, the Patriots need to generate some run-game efficiency with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to get the Bills out of two-deep coverage. The Patriots are averaging 3.9 YPC (20th in the league) with an explosive run rate of 8.2% (25th). No question on the numbers here. They are down. Let's see how McDaniels game-plans for Jim Leonhard and the Bills' new defensive scheme to get his QB rolling again. And it wouldn't surprise me if the Patriots try to muddy this one up with a ball control/play-action script. Now, let's get to some prop bets ... James Cook III is coming off two straight big rushing performances and is averaging 6.0 YPC. AP Photo/Adrian Kraus James Cook III rushing yards OVER 88.5 (-111) As mentioned, Cook has rushed for 135-plus in two straight, and he's averaging 19.3 carries per game. Plus, Cook has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season. Take the steady volume and the explosive-play ability here. Hunter Henry receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-110) Henry has topped the 31-yard mark just once this season, and he was held to just one reception in the Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. However, I see the tight end as an answer to the two-high zone coverage of the Bills. Henry can be the outlet for Maye, while also pressing the seams. DJ Moore receptions OVER 3.5 (-133) The juice isn't friendly on this one, but that's a low reception total for Moore. In the two full games Moore has played (he left Week 2 early with an injury), he had at least five receptions in both. Look for the Bills to use motion to deploy Moore, getting him free access off the ball versus man coverage. There's a good chance of rain showers Sunday night, and we know that Jared Goff 's performance as a passer can be impacted more by bad weather, given his smaller hands. But I still feel comfortable taking this bet at this number because of the Panthers' injury issues. Both starting cornerbacks are expected to miss this game, which all but precludes Carolina from playing man coverage against Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams . If the Panthers take a zone-heavy approach, expect Jahmyr Gibbs to run wild -- heck, expect Gibbs to run wild anyway, as the Panthers are giving up more rushing yards per game to running backs than any other defense. Detroit's defense is extremely gettable through the air, but the Lions have enough pass rush power to generate sacks and turnovers such that the Panthers can't keep this shootout within one score. DeVonta Smith missed practice Thursday with his hamstring injury, which officially moves him into the "seriously questionable" category as we approach Sunday. I already leaned to the Rams' side with a healthy Smith. If he can't go, the Eagles' receiver corps will feature Dontayvion Wicks , first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown against the loaded Rams secondary. Remember, pass-catching tight end Dallas Goedert is also out with a knee injury. The Eagles' defense had a brutal night last Monday against the Chicago Bears ' passing attack, regularly suffering communication issues as the Bears sent receivers in motion. They get another motion-heavy passing attack in Sean McVay's Rams offense, which gets Puka Nacua back at a critical time -- at 1-2, the Rams need a road win to prevent the sirens from screaming in their Super Bowl-aspiring season. They also have a vengeance play here, as they gave up a big second-half lead to the Eagles last season ... then lost the game on a would-be game-winning field goal that was blocked by Jordan Davis . The Eagles simply have too many personnel deficiencies to ignore against a team as deep and talented as the Rams. Get this line before Smith news pushes it higher before kickoff. Miami Dolphins team total points UNDER 13.5 (-115) Minnesota Vikings DC Brian Flores is calling defense for the first time against his old team. He has downplayed the importance of facing Miami, but I'd imagine the leaders in the locker room know how big of a game this is for their top-flight coordinator. I also think this is about as big of a mismatch as we will see this season. The Dolphins are without running back De'Von Achane , who provided much-needed game-breaking ability from the running back spot. Without him, the Dolphins' best chance for chunk gains will come from the passing game, which is a scary proposition against Flores' blitz-heavy approach. Bobby Slowik, the new offensive coordinator in Miami, lost his job in Houston in large part due to predictable protection rules that were easily exploited by opposing defensive coordinators -- and no coach has been better attacking the Mike Shanahan system in pass protection than Flores. I'm tracking under 13.5 at -115 for a full unit and under 7.5 points at +285 for a half unit. A shutout at 13-1 would be fun, but that's too short of a price to take seriously. Make Your Picks Hampton's share of carries took a hit last week, as he saw 57.7% of the designed rushes after holding 76.7% and 75.0% in the first two weeks of the season, respectively. The Los Angeles Chargers wanted to get Keaton Mitchell more involved as they looked for any sort of juice on offense, and it was a better day for the running game overall. I expect a time share moving forward. But it will be a tough test against the Seattle Seahawks , who boast the best run-defending line in football. There might be no greater mismatch in Week 4 than the Chargers' interior offensive line against defensive tackles Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams . If the Chargers are to find any success on the ground, they'll need to get the ball to the boundary -- those are the Mitchell plays, not the Hampton plays. The Chargers were able to run the ball a lot more last week as they tripped into an early lead after the Bills' many turnovers, but it's more likely they get stuck in a trailing game script in this one. Hampton has big-play ability if he breaks into space, so taking the under on attempts might be a safer approach. I didn't want to pay the juice at under 13.5 attempts at -123 as of this posting, but if under 12.5 appears, I'll be interested in taking that. Kaleb Johnson rushing attempts OVER 8.5 (-115) The Green Bay Packers ' lack of a handoff game is harrowing. Through three games, the Packers have 146 total rushing yards from running backs -- eighth fewest for a team through three games over the past six seasons. The one-dimensionality on offense particularly haunted them against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night, but they've had a long week to explore offensive line reinforcements and recommit to the rushing attack. Green Bay has the fifth-highest pass rate over expectation per Next Gen Stats. Behind that offensive line? No shot. They need to find a rushing attack, and they know it. Critically, the Packers draw a rookie UDFA quarterback ( Jalon Daniels ) making his first career start for a bad Tampa Bay Buccaneers team. The potential to build an actual lead and salt it away should also increase the total handoffs in this game. The Packers clearly don't trust MarShawn Lloyd as a ball carrier, and Chris Brooks is the third-down back. If the running game plays a bigger role this week in a leading game script, Johnson is the most likely beneficiary. I prefer Johnson's attempts to his yardage totals, simply because the Packers' line is still a problem. But both are bettable as his role expands. Woody Marks rushing yards OVER 33.5 (-114) NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks Our Dan Graziano reported this week that his sense of the Houston Texans ' running game is that more work should go Marks' way . I'm inclined to agree. David Montgomery is a good stay-ahead-of-the-sticks rusher, but with Houston's offensive line issues, he has been unable to solve their short-yardage problems on his own. By getting the ball to Marks on the outside, the Texans can find bigger runs without worrying as much about their interior offensive line play. The Dallas Cowboys have given up 114.3 rushing yards per game to running backs through three weeks, fifth worst in the league. They have played three mobile QBs ( Jaxson Dart , Jayden Daniels , Lamar Jackson ) who make run defense more challenging, but the eye test confirms the liability of players like outside linebackers Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku in setting a hard edge. With Nico Collins back in the starting lineup for Houston, the temptation is to think the Texans will become more pass-heavy -- but their offensive philosophy this season was always to give C.J. Stroud a better running game. I'd take Marks to 36.5 this week, and I'd look at some longest rush props as well. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Zay Flowers receiving yards OVER 66.5 (-110) I had all sorts of Flowers overs to target against the Cowboys last week, but his hamstring injury limited him to just 15 routes. Of course, he still went over his yardage prop with 84 yards on only 15 routes. Flowers is a huge-play star-in-the-making in this Declan Doyle offense, and the books still haven't caught up. Flowers has now only played 1.5 games of football through three weeks, and four of those six quarters were with load management. Yet, he has 234 receiving yards and a whopping 9.36 yards per route run because of how easily the Baltimore Ravens are getting him open with motion, backfield alignment and play-action pass fakes. He's as central to this passing attack as Jaxon Smith-Njigba is to Seattle's, and as he strings together full healthy games, we'll never see a number in the 60s for him again. If you're worried about continued management on the hamstring injury, especially in a game the Ravens might dominate, consider taking Flowers' first-quarter receiving props (over 14.5 receiving yards is +100) to ensure the Ravens are still in their base offense. Michael Mayer receiving yards OVER 21.5 (-116) In Brock Bowers ' first game back healthy, Mayer's route share was totally unaffected. Mayer ran a route on 71% of the Las Vegas Raiders ' dropbacks in Week 1, 72% in Week 2, and 70% in Week 3. That's because the Raiders are using Bowers like a true wide receiver. They were in multiple-TE sets on over 80% of their total snaps, and with Bowers typically in slot or wide alignments, Mayer got the matchups against linebackers and safeties from his traditional inline alignments. Throw in the fact that the Raiders' traditional wide receivers are a thin group without much demand for targets, and I still think Mayer is the second target after Bowers. As opposing defenses spend more resources to take Bowers out of the game plan, it's Mayer who will benefit. The Raiders have a good shot of a trailing game script against the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs' run-heavy approach shortens the clock and makes it a little tougher to take receptions, so I prefer receiving yards here. But if we get into a big score deficit in the second half, I'll look for a live receptions over on Mayer. Their pass rush win rate tells a similar story; it ranks 25th best. Now, the Cardinals' pass protection has also not been good this year, ranking second worst in pass block win rate. Despite that, they have allowed sacks on just 4.1% of dropbacks, better than the league average of 6.0%. My model believes their chances of giving up a sack on their opening drive is quite a bit lower than these odds suggest. Greg Rousseau under 0.75 sacks (+147) Rousseau is having an unbelievable start to the season, with 6.0 sacks in three games. One factor is the quarterback he's facing: Lamar Jackson . The Ravens' quarterback has taken sacks at an average-ish 5.7% clip this year, but my model isn't ready to totally forget the massive 9.8% number he recorded a year ago. And even if you don't think Johnson is great -- and I don't -- he's still on the field on 66% of the Titans' pass rushes and 77% in clear passing situations. This line is too good to pass up. I would bet this down to +175. Other sack bets I recommend: Arden Key over 0.25 sacks (+197) Abdul Carter over 0.25 sacks (+109) Dayo Odeyingbo under 0.25 sacks (-135) Jeffery Simmons over 0.25 sacks (+112) Donovan Ezeiruaku over 0.25 sacks (+249) Danielle Hunter under 0.75 sacks (-108) Andrew Van Ginkel under 0.75 sacks (-107) Leonard Williams under 0.75 sacks (-108) George Karlaftis over 0.25 sacks (+224) Aidan Hutchinson under 0.75 sacks (+131) Brandon Jones under 6.5 tackles + assists (+103) Jones is recording a tackle on 16% of opponent run plays and 8% of opponent pass plays. It's the first number that stands out, because it ranks in the 84th percentile among safeties. But here's the thing: the 49ers have been pass-heavy this season! They literally rank first in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. And every time a Broncos opponent opts to pass instead of run, that cuts Jones' chances of recording a tackle roughly in half. That's one reason why my model likes Jones' under quite a bit. I would bet this down to -132. Roquan Smith over 7.5 tackles + assists (+102) This is a low tackle line for Smith to clear, considering he's gone over 7.5 in each of his three games this season and nine out of 15 last year. On one hand, we can understand why: the Ravens are huge favorites over the Titans, and so the game script expectation is that Tennessee will fall behind and be forced to pass. For a linebacker like Smith, that would be bad for his tackling numbers since he's much more likely to record one against the run. But working in our favor is that Tennessee has been extremely run heavy thus far, ranking 31st in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. Other tackle bets I recommend: Reed Blankenship under 6.5 tackles + assists (-117) Fred Warner under 8.5 tackles + assists (+104) Pat Surtain II under 4.5 tackles + assists (-102) Deommodore Lenoir under 5.5 tackles + assists (-124) Ji'Ayir Brown over 4.5 tackles + assists (-118) Offensive plays Jordan Love pass attempts UNDER 35.5 (-119) The Green Bay Packers have been pass-heavy in 2026, with the sixth-highest pass rate over expectation according to NFL Next Gen Stats. My attempts model assumes that is going to come down, because leaning that heavily on the pass game is not what the Packers have done in the past under Matt LaFleur. Green Bay ranked 26th in the same category last season. But there's also this: The Packers' offensive line has struggled immensely. I can only imagine they would want to limit the number of times Love drops back on Sunday, especially against Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles, who loves to blitz. Jaylen Wright receptions OVER 1.5 (+180) Wright and Ollie Gordon II will handle the backfield workload in the wake of De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL injury. Both have almost no experience catching the ball in the pros, but someone is going to have to catch passes out of the backfield -- and that's especially true this week. That's because the Miami Dolphins are playing the Minnesota Vikings, one of the most zone-heavy teams in the league (78% zone). Running backs catch passes against zone coverage almost twice as frequently compared to when they face man coverage, and in my back tests, betting the receptions over on running backs facing zone-heavy defenses has been profitable. Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. I have seven picks I like this week, including player props on Patrick Mahomes , Drake Maye , and Tony Pollard , plus three spreads picks for the 1 PM Eastern games. Best of luck, happy November, and enjoy your day! Vikings at Lions (-3): O/U 46.5 I said Monday of this week on NBC that this was the no-brainer of the week. It’s a miracle that the Minnesota Vikings are the lone undefeated team in the NFL, and to me, they are the most overrated team. In the last four games, Minnesota has beaten Tampa Bay, Miami, New Orleans, and Indianapolis; those teams are a combined 7-20. Last season, the Vikings swept the Lions in the regular season, and adding Kyler Murray likely doesn’t equate to another sweep over Detroit. Murray ranks 21st and 26th in passer rating against man and zone coverage, 28th in blitzed completion percentage (54.8%), and 26th in play-action completion percentage (54.9%). On early downs, Minnesota ranks in success rate, while Detroit is first. Going score for score on the road as an underdog with Jared Goff and the Lions doesn’t seem plausible to me. I like Detroit -3 at -120 odds. Pick: Lions -3 (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Titans at Bengals (-12.5): O/U 46.5 Tony Pollard had a season-high 129 rushing yards on 25 carries and tied a career-high with three rushing touchdowns. It was a great day for Pollard, but the Titans lost at the buzzer 27-24 to the Browns. Now, Tennessee goes on the road as double-digit underdogs in Cincinnati. Not a recipe for success. Last week, Pollard had an amazing game script to be fed, maybe the best he’s had all year, but I don’t see it this week, especially going up against Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen . The Bengals held Derrick Henry to 45 rushing yards on 17 carries last week, and with Cam Ward striking no fear in the Bengals’ hearts, I’d think Cincy stacks the box and attempt to take Pollard out of the equation. I went Under 65.5 rushing yards on Pollard and would go down to 60.5. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 65.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Browns at Steelers (-3.5): O/U 38.5 I still can’t believe my eyes and ears regarding the Cleveland Browns being 5-2! But all good things must come to an end, right? All five of Cleveland’s wins have come by four or fewer points, and they needed a walkoff field goal to beat the Titans in Tennessee and the same at home against the Ravens in the last two weeks. Cleveland has been playing with fire recently, while the Steelers were spotted flying back from Paris playing with ice. Aaron Rodgers was wearing chains that cost more than my house and probably yours too on that flight back from the NFL’s first-ever game in Paris. Rodgers said it was his favorite road flight of his lengthy NFL career, and the Steelers are starting to hit their stride with three-straight wins following the loss to the Browns in Cleveland. The Steelers traveling back to an immediate game is worrisome because the last eight teams that played in London, then a game in the States the following week, went 0-8 ATS! However, the Browns haven’t swept the Steelers in the regular season since 1988. It’s a revenge spot for Pittsburgh, and if you’ve seen the back-and-forth between Cam Heyward and Jared Verse this week, then you know it’s going to be a classic AFC North slugfest. Give me Pittsburgh at home -3.5. I’d prefer a -3, but the sportsbooks are playing more defense than ever this season. Pick: Steelers -3.5 (1 unit) Falcons at Bucs (-2.5): O/U Tampa Bay got that Baker bump last week! Baker Mayfield came back from injury and Tampa Bay looked inspired. The Bucs rattled Bryce Young last week and destroyed his confidence turning three turnovers into 17 of the teams 43 points. This week won’t be so easy hosting Atlanta in a letdown spot off the hype. Mayfield only threw the ball 11 times, so we truly don’t know how healthy he is or how effective he will be, but we know what to expect from Atlanta. The Falcons have the fifth-best offensive success rate since Michael Penix has taken over, and he’s gotten the ball out quick with 50% of his passes coming within 2.5 seconds (fourth-best). That could be the key against a blitz and pressure heavy Bucs defense. Tampa Bay loads the box with eight or more players at the second-highest clip (22.1%) and blitzes 40.4% of the time when doing so, which ranks fifth-most. I’d expect a lot of screens, draws, and quick throws to offeset the Bucs defense, while Atlanta likely brings pressure and tries to hit Mayfield as many times as possible to truly test his health and conditioning. Give me Atlanta. Pick: Falcons +2.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Patriots (-7) at Dolphins: O/U 43.5 Last season, Drake Maye completed 33-of-41 (80.5%) passes for 421 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions over two wins against Miami. Maye even added 72 rushing yards and another score on 15 carries in those two outings. This Miami defense is even less menacing than last year. The Dolphins have four interceptions on the season, and two came in Week 1 against Kirk Cousins , with another last week courtesy of Geno Smith . When Joe Burrow , Patrick Mahomes , Brock Purdy , and Kyler Murray played Miami, that group averaged 242.5 passing yards against the Dolphins and combined for eight touchdown passes to one interception. Kyler Murray was the only quarterback who hasn’t thrown at least two touchdowns against Miami. At -102 odds, I like Maye to go Under 0.5 Interceptions versus Miami for a third consecutive time and like 2+ Pass touchdowns for parlays. Pick: Drake Maye Under 0.5 Interceptions (1 unit) Chiefs (-1.5) at Broncos: O/U 40.5 In Week 1 against Denver, Patrick Mahomes came back from a major surgery and finished with 184 passing yards, 15-of-27 passing, and three total touchdowns, including an epic rushing score to start the game. He went Under all of his props except passing touchdowns and rushing yards. Fast forward to last week, Mahomes had his worst game of the season on Sunday Night Football against the defending Super Bowl Champion Seahawks in Seattle. Mahomes turns around and goes to Denver to face a Broncos defense that almost went to the Super Bowl. It’s going to be a long day for the Chiefs, but unless Kenneth Walker goes crazy again (191 total yards, 2 TDs) this looks like a spot for Mahomes to go over his props. The Broncos average 5.1 plays per possession, ranking worst in the NFL. That’s one area that points toward more plays and possessions for the Chiefs. Both of these teams rarely allow sacks or turn the ball over, so we should see plenty of possessions. Both teams had 12 drives in Week 1’s meeting, and Kansas City ran 20 more plays than Denver (62-42) thanks to the running game, and it was Davis Webb ‘s first game as an OC with the Broncos. Still, Kansas City will likely run more plays and have more possessions than Denver. Denver got back Jonathan Cooper last week, plus Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga could both play today. The Denver defense has usually limited the touchdown damage through the air from Mahomes, but in order to move the ball against Denver’s defense, Mahomes will have to be actively taking what the Broncos can give him. I like Mahomes to go Over 20.5 completions and 220.5 paassing yards up to 21.5 and 225.5. I lean his Over pass attempts. Without further ado, here are three of the best player props for NFL Week 1, including Garrett Wilson, David Montgomery and Omarion Hampton. *]:mx-auto lg:[&>*]:mx-0"> Best NFL Player Prop Bets and Picks for Week 1 David Montgomery Anytime TD (-120) David Montgomery has found a new home in Houston. The Lions’ “Sonic and Knuckles” duo in the backfield was one of the best in the league over the past few years. However, Montgomery was always second fiddle to Jahmyr Gibbs in Detroit. He was always productive, especially in the red zone, but now he has the chance to be the RB1 for the Texans. Over the past three seasons, Montgomery has scored 33 touchdowns on the ground, despite being in that backup role. Now, he should get almost all of the touches when Houston is in the scoring area. The Bills had an awful run defense last season. They ranked 31st in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 25th in defensive rushing success rate. This Houston team has struggled with pass protection over the past couple of seasons, so it should try to take advantage of that poor run defense and get the ball to Montgomery whenever possible. David Montgomery should start his Houston tenure with a touchdown. Garrett Wilson 6+ Receptions (-121) During the offseason, new Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall as the Jets’ “bell cows.” The Jets aren’t a great team, but they know they have two very reliable and dangerous weapons in Wilson and Hall. To make things easy on Geno Smith, Reich will want to scheme ways to get the ball to those two players as often as possible. Wilson dealt with an injury that kept him out for most of last season, but in the first six games of the season when he was fit, Wilson had at least six catches in four of those six games. Geno Smith did not have a good season in Las Vegas, but he had a terrible offensive line and a bad group of skill position players. He might not get back to the guy he was in Seattle, but he should have a much better season with an underrated Jets offensive line protecting him. Smith might have turnover issues, but he is not afraid to let it fly. Since the start of the 2022 season, he ranks fourth in the NFL in pass attempts. This Titans defense is very vulnerable, and Frank Reich should let Geno Smith chuck it early and often in this game. This is a good early matchup for Smith to get his feet under him in a Jets uniform (for the second time) and feed his WR1 Garrett Wilson. This is a good matchup for him to start the season against the Cardinals. Last season, Arizona ranked 22nd in the NFL in defensive EPA/rush and 23rd in defensive rushing success rate. My Week 5 betting card finished 7-4 (4-2 on sides/totals and 3-2 on player props), marking five straight weeks in the black. Over five weeks, the official plays went 7-4, 6-5, 6-4, 6-5 and 7-4. We are 32-22 overall for a strong 59% hit rate. The best of the bunch was the Packers as home underdogs against the Bears. I called that one a lock, and Green Bay won outright, 31-7. Divisional home underdogs? Trust the process. The Steelers laying a field goal and the Bills Moneyline in overtime against the Rams cashed, too. I was kicking myself for not making the Steelers a top pick on the Best Bets Show ahead of Week 5 - given that Indianapolis was coming off an international game and had no bye week. The one that stung was the Eagles-Jaguars spread: Jacksonville won, but only by two points. But I survived my back-to-back double-header wedding weekend (again, congrats to my sister, Rachael, and new big brother-in-law Matt, and my close friends, Mollie and Mike). Let's get back to business with all remaining games for Week 16 featured below (including the Sunday Night Football and Monday Night Football matchups). More NFL Betting Advice NFL Prop Bet Cheat Sheet Expert NFL Game Picks NFL Betting Strategy Best +EV NFL Picks Get instant alerts when a line reaches your target via the BettingPros App >> Two things stand out in the league-wide trends heading into Week 6. First, prime-time underdogs have covered nine straight games, and all nine won outright. Tampa Bay, Baltimore and Buffalo kept it going last week. Dallas-Green Bay on Sunday night and Washington-San Francisco on Monday night are the next tests. Second, the home-underdog edge cooled off slightly. After starting the season 14-8-1 ATS, home underdogs went just 1-4-1 in Week 5 and sit at 15-12-2 against the spread (ATS) for the season, a bit under 56% of decided bets. They still have won 12 out of 29 games outright (41%). Divisional home underdogs are still the sweet spot at 6-2 ATS (5-3 straight up). Based on the early lines, the Week 6 slate has home underdogs in the Buccaneers (vs. Steelers), Browns (vs. Ravens, in-division), Giants (vs. Saints), Falcons (vs. Bears) and Raiders (vs. Bills), and possibly the Packers if the Cowboys stay favored. The Browns-Ravens game is the only divisional game of the group. A reminder that Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on bye, so we have 14 games this week, excluding Thursday’s Seahawks-Broncos matchup. We took the Seahawks laying less than a field goal. And it hit, despite Bo Nix’s horrific performance; Seattle fell short in overtime in Denver. After Week 6, prime-time underdogs have covered in 10 straight games, and all 10 won outright. Pretty crazy. League-Wide Trends Week 5 Recap Favorites went 7-7-1 ATS; underdogs went 7-7-1 ATS (15 games). Home teams went 4-9-1 ATS; road teams went 9-4-1 ATS (one neutral-site game excluded). Home underdogs went 1-4-1 ATS (the Packers covered and won outright; the Dolphins pushed at -7). Overall O/U: 8-7. Full Season 2026 (through Week 5) Favorites went 34-40-5 ATS; underdogs went 40-34-5 ATS (79 games). Home teams went 36-35-4 ATS; road teams went 35-36-4 ATS (4 neutral-site games excluded). Overall O/U: 39-40. Home Underdogs (through Week 5) Home underdogs are 15-12-2 ATS (29 games; neutral-site games excluded), which is 55.6% of decided bets. Home underdogs have won 12 of those 29 games outright (41%), and the OVER went 14-15. Divisional home underdogs are 6-2 ATS (5-3 straight up); all divisional underdogs are 14-4 ATS (18 games). Prime-Time Highlight (Wed Opener/TNF/SNF/MNF, through Week 5) Favorites went 3-12-1 ATS; underdogs went 12-3-1 ATS (16 games). Home teams went 8-6-1 ATS; road teams went 6-8-1 ATS (one neutral-site game excluded). Overall O/U: 9-7. Streaks: Prime-time underdogs have covered in nine straight games (and won all nine outright, dating back to Falcons-Packers in Week 3). Prime-time home teams have failed to cover in four straight. The OVER has hit in the last two prime-time games. For my thoughts on all the games on the Week 6 slate, be sure to check out the weekly lookahead lines show I do every week with Ryan Wormley (Monday release following every Sunday slate) on the BettingPros YouTube Channel. Arizona is 2-0 ATS in 2026 when catching eight or more points: +9.5 at the Chargers in Week 1 (a 26-14 outright win) and +8.5 at San Francisco in Week 3 (a 36-30 loss). New injury: McVay said Trent McDuffie's groin 'felt something' after practice on Thursday and will not practice Friday out of caution. — Michael J. Duarte (@michaeljduarte) October 16, 2026 Betting Preview I think 12.5 is too big a number. That is the biggest number the Rams have laid this year (with no home-field advantage to factor in). Short week after an overtime loss against a head coach, Mike LaFleur, who spent three years with the Rams as their offensive coordinator. The Rams will also be without starting left tackle Alaric Jackson because of a one-game suspension. The Rams have failed to cover the spread with a rest disadvantage in the last four instances. Against that line, the Rams would have covered one of five games this season, the +22 over the Giants, while Arizona would have covered three times. Arizona is 2-0 ATS in 2026 when getting eight or more points. The risk is that Arizona has lost by 24 twice (Weeks 2 and 5) and allows 32.4 points per game. Woof . It’s scary because the Cardinals are willing to drop back and throw 40 to 45 times per game with a combination of Jacoby Brissett/Michael Wilson/Trey McBride, and that creates garbage-time opportunities. I like the value with Arizona at this number. Arizona’s biggest cover this season came in Week 1 at the Chargers in Los Angeles, where the Cardinals were 9.5-point underdogs and won outright, and I’ll take them playing in Los Angeles again. This is also one of those classic “close your eyes” specials: Team gets blown out by 21+ points one week, then catches double-digit points the following week, etc. This matchup doesn’t align with the official “close your eyes” special (21 points versus the spread, so technically the Raiders qualify this week after getting blown out by New England), but you catch my drift. Even so… The Cardinals got blown out twice last year by the Rams, 37-20 and 45-17, but I think we can all agree that last year’s Rams team might be better than the 2026 version. L.A. covered the double-digit spread in both games, although Arizona was winning late into the third quarter in the second matchup. If you can’t stomach the Cardinals, the over is another option. Four of the last five games between these two teams have gone over the closing line total. The Raiders’ loss to the Patriots said more about the Patriots than the Raiders. Las Vegas is very boom-or-bust on defense, and when its pressure doesn’t get home, it gives up explosive downfield plays. Drake Maye had plenty of time to throw, even after Will Campbell got hurt. When you play the Buffalo Bills, saddle up, as there are going to be a lot of explosive plays. Josh Allen indoors is a rare occurrence, and I expect it to remind us how much fun he is on fast turf with all of these playmakers. Buffalo games average 61.0 combined points and are 4-1 to the Over. Las Vegas games average 52.2, and the Raiders are on a three-game Over streak. Seth Woolcock dropped this as one of his best bets for Week 6, riding the over in Sin City. I tend to agree, given that these high-total games have not closed high enough so far this season. Through Week 5, games with a closing total of 50+ points are 7-2 to the Over (78%). Dropping the cutoff to 49.5 makes it 9-2 across 11 games. Overall: across all road games, 1-1 ATS and 1-1 O/U; across all games as an underdog, 1-0-1 ATS and 2-0 O/U; across all 2026 games, 2-2-1 ATS and 3-2 O/U. Dallas streaks through Week 5: 2-3 straight up (one-game losing streak), 2-2-1 against the spread (one-game non-cover streak), 3-2 toward the total (one-game Under streak). Green Bay streaks through Week 5: 3-2 straight up (two-game win streak), 1-3-1 against the spread (one-game cover streak), 2-3 toward the total (two-game Under streak). Dallas comes in off a 24-16 home loss to Tampa Bay as an 8.5-point favorite, failing to cover (Week 5). Green Bay comes in off a 31-7 home win over Chicago as a 1.5-point underdog, covering (Week 5). Green Bay ended a 0-9-1 ATS skid (10 straight games without a cover) in Week 5, a 31-7 win over Chicago as a 1.5-point home underdog. Green Bay is 5-11 ATS as a favorite since 2025 (the Week 4 game at Tampa Bay, a push at -3, is not counted). Dallas is 2-3-1 ATS and 3-3 O/U over its last six games (2025 Week 18 through 2026 Week 5); Green Bay is 1-4-1 ATS and 3-3 O/U over its last six games (2025 Wild Card Round through 2026 Week 5). Injuries Brandon Cisse added to the injury report and is questionable. pic.twitter.com/ByPqPtKkwm — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 16, 2026 Betting Preview This has to be a shootout, right? The last time these teams met was a 40-40 tie on Sunday Night Football last year. In the last six games these teams have played, the total has gone Over. As for sides… I’ll take the team with the points, the Cowboys, as painful as that sounds after taking them to cover and win outright last week against the Buccaneers, and then watching them lose outright. In retrospect, why would I think they could cover that line? Anytime they are heavy favorites, you fade them to oblivion, and anytime they get written off as underdogs, that is when you want to be on their side. I also don’t think Green Bay has totally erased its issues. The offensive line is still really bad, and you saw the cracks up front at times against Jordan Love when the Bears’ pressure got home. When it didn’t, he was able to rip off explosive plays, which he will be able to do against Dallas too. It will be back-and-forth and come down to the last possession, so I’ll take the team catching the points with Dak Prescott as a slight underdog (7-2 ATS as an underdog since 2025, second-best mark in the NFL). Conversely, you never want to bet on the Packers as favorites in any capacity… they are 6-11 ATS as a favorite since last season (0-2-1 this season), fresh off their first cover in their last 10 games. Don’t let Week 5 change your entire outlook on both of these teams. Not to mention… the prime-time underdogs this season have covered 10 straight games, and won all of them outright. Back to the total briefly, because there’s a chance of some wind in the forecast that bettors should be wary of. Gusts up to 27 miles per hour (MPH) could be problematic, so be sure to do your due diligence before firing on the game total. And the full integration of Joey Porter Jr. could eventually turn the tide of the Dallas defense starting in Week 6. Meanwhile, Green Bay could be down another cornerback in Brandon Cisse. Christian Watson has scored the first touchdown in his last three home games with Jordan Love as his quarterback (Green Bay has scored the first touchdown in six straight games). That was Welsh’s favorite first touchdown call on our Week 6 Props Show. I already mentioned my first touchdown call, but I’m still interested in touchdown props for this game. Let me introduce Packers wide receiver J. Michael Sturdivant. He caught a 43-yard touchdown last week that was overturned on an offensive pass interference call. But the coaches acknowledged this week that it would have been awesome to get him his first touchdown, but that it will be coming pretty soon (S/O The Coachspeak Index). Props Christian Watson First Touchdown Scorer (+1000) J. Michael Sturdivant Anytime Touchdown Scorer (+1050) NFL Monday Night Football Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers Betting Lines & Odds Erickson’s Pick: 49ers -7.5 Trends As a road underdog (the role it plays here), Washington is 1-1 ATS (50%) and 2-0 O/U in 2026. Washington streaks through Week 5: 1-3-1 straight up (last game was a tie; no active win/loss streak), 2-3 against the spread (two-game non-cover streak), 4-1 toward the total (one-game Over streak). San Francisco streaks through Week 5: 5-0 straight up (five-game win streak), 4-1 against the spread (two-game cover streak), 3-2 toward the total (one-game Over streak). Washington comes in off a 27-27 tie with the Giants as a 3.5-point favorite, failing to cover (Week 5). San Francisco comes in off a 32-29 road win at Seattle as a 3-point underdog, covering (Week 5). San Francisco had gone Over the total in each of its previous five games as a favorite before the Week 4 game against Denver went Under (24-14, 38 points vs. 48.5). Washington is 3-3 ATS and 4-2 O/U over its last six games (2025 Week 18 through 2026 Week 5); San Francisco is 4-2 ATS and 4-2 O/U over its last six games (2025 Divisional Round through 2026 Week 5). Washington games are averaging 52.8 combined points in 2026 (264 in five games), and San Francisco games are averaging 49.4 (247 in five games). Prime-time record in 2026 (through Week 5): Washington has not played a prime-time game in 2026; San Francisco is 1-0 ATS and 0-1 O/U in 1 prime-time game. Injuries There's a growing possibility that the 49ers may be without Mike Evans & Nick Bosa vs the #Commanders pic.twitter.com/hNUbIL5LlG — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) October 16, 2026 Betting Preview Originally, I wanted to back the Commanders. Getting more than a touchdown with Jayden Daniels, a quarterback who performs well when his team is the underdog, is appealing, and he looked fantastic running the ball in his return last week versus the New York Giants (despite also taking five sacks). But this Washington defense is so bad that Kyle Shanahan, Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and whoever else is healthy are going to have a field day against it. The biggest difference in the 49ers’ defense is linebacker Fred Warner. Warner is the tide that lifts all boats, and he can spy Daniels as a runner, which is what concerns me about backing Washington. If he slows Daniels down on the ground, you are left needing Washington’s offense to pass its way back, and the Commanders can’t consistently run the ball behind a shaky offensive line that traveled cross-country after an overtime tie. I usually don’t like laying this many points with the 49ers, so in the early look this was a shy-away spot for me. But upon further research, the 49ers’ 10-3-1 mark ATS as a favorite ranks No. 1 in the NFL since 2025. It’s not as great at home (4-3-1), but positive nonetheless. San Francisco as a favorite is still a lean I like, and I’d rather be with the 49ers than the Commanders. It’s rare to see an injury report for a 49ers game when they look like the healthiest team. I’m treating it as a lean rather than a play at this number. My favorite play in this game is betting against the Commanders quarterback and his legs. The 49ers are allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game to quarterbacks, including mobile quarterbacks like Malik Willis and Bo Nix. They combined for 16 yards. No quarterback has rushed for more than 10 yards against the 49ers this season, with four out of five going Under their rushing projection. Willis had six rushing yards on a 37.5-yard rushing prop. Daniels has recorded 201 yards on scrambles this season, second-most in the NFL, and has averaged a league-leading 12.6 yards per carry on those runs (minimum five carries). The 49ers’ defense has faced five scrambles, tied for the fewest in the NFL, and has allowed 5.6 yards per carry on those runs (6th-fewest) according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Here are my best bets for the Sunday and Monday slate in the NFL Week 9. Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings. Best of luck! Bengals (-3.5) vs Falcons: O/U 52.5 The Bengals and Falcons kick off in Madrid, Spain, at 9:30 AM Eastern Sunday morning, so set your alarm clocks, aka your phones! This should be a fantastic matchup, and I am looking at the Atlanta offense for a bounce-back spot. Last week against Tampa Bay, the Falcons lost in a monsoon as Michael Penix threw four interceptions, while the Atlanta defense was run. In sunny weather, we should expect the Falcons to look night and day. The Bengals are on a three-game winning streak over Miami, Baltimore, and Tennessee. Cam Ward threw for 304 yards and touchdowns, plus Tony Pollard ran for 117 yards and two scores on the Bengals. The Bengals’ four wins all come against teams with losing records so far, while the Falcons have shown their potential with wins over Green Bay and San Francisco. I still think the Falcons have the highest ceiling in the NFC South. I’ll take the +3.5 down to +3. Pick: Falcons +3.5 (1 unit) Giants (-3) at Eagles: O/U 38.5 For the first time since November 1, 2009, the New York Giants are favorites in Philadelphia, and that’s no mistake. Things are so bad during the Eagles’ six-game losing streak that they’ve benched Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton . Philadelphia has a bye week up next, so this is them 100-percent trying to see what they have before they decide on their intentions in the second half of the season. If the Eagles lose this game, they are borderline out of the postseason before Week 11 starts, but that desperation doesn’t interest me because they haven’t had any rhythm amid all the injuries. The Giants, on the other hand, are in first place in the division, coming out of a bye week after an impressive 27-21 OT win over Houston. New York has found something with J.J. McCarthy , and if Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers are bought in like they were against Houston (232 combined yards), then so am I. I like the Giants -3. Pick: Giants -3 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Packers at Patriots (-3): O/U 44.5 Green Bay has averaged a league-high 81.7% of their yards through the air, and 65.7% of their plays are passes. At some point, regression has to hit, and the backfield becomes more reliable. Josh Jacobs has started to turn the wheels of regression, but as we’ve seen through two games, it may take time. This matchup will be interesting since New England runs the third-most man coverage (29%). Love has completed 51% of his passes against man (25th) for 6.2 yards per attempt (6.2). Love’s faced a slew of bad defenses this season, and New England certainly isn’t bad. Christian Watson is a go, so I expect plenty of passes, but 37.5 is still steep despite Love throwing 41-plus times in three straight. I am going to sell high on Love and also go under Matthew Golden ‘s 68.5 receiving yards. Last week, Watson was very active before he suffered an injury that opened the door for Golden to sneak over his yards prop. Golden has gone over his yards prop in three of his last four games and saw 12-plus targets in three straight. However, Golden ranks 66th in target separation versus man coverage, and going up Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis III won’t be easy. I’m going under on both Love and Golden. Picks: Jordan Love Under 37.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 69.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Cardinals at Seahawks (-8.5): O/U 39.5 Last week, I lost on Jaxon Smith-Njigba Under 101.5 receiving yards in garbage time, but you better believe I am running it back. JSN has been nothing short of spectacular. If the season ended today, he is the Offensive Player of the Year. JSN leads the league in receiving yards (985) and receiving touchdowns (9). He has four straight games with 100-plus receiving yards and seven out of eight on the season, but I am going Under. Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett away and will roll with Gardner Minshew for the meantime. Sam Darnold is out for Seattle, so Drew Lock will step up. Luckily for Lock, Seattle’s backfield is more crowded than ever and willing to assist. Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet both returned in the last two weeks, plus George Holani and Emmanuel Wilson are capable backs. Arizona has lost 10 straight to Seattle, and after selling this past week, I could see the Seahawks rolling and working on their ground game. In Week 2 against Arizona with Lock at quarterback, Seattle ran the ball 40 times and threw it 26. JSN caught 155 of Lock’s 235 yards (11 targets). Ridiculous, but we could see a similar result here in play calling, capping JSN’s production. Pick: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Under 94.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Buccaneers at Bears (-6): O/U 47.5 Baker Mayfield has had the easiest job in the NFL over the last two weeks. Mayfield has thrown 14 passes in past two games. Against Atlanta, Mayfield and the Bucs became the first quarterback/team to not complete a pass since September 29, 1974! Mayfield went 0-for-3 and we might not see that feat happen for another 50 years. However, the good days are over. Welcome to the end times, Baker. You are in Chicago facing a white-hot Bears team with additions on the defense from trades and guys returning from injury. Mayfield won’t have the liberty of handing the ball to his talented backs like he has literally over 100 times in the last two games. I like all of Mayfield’s Overs this week, but my favorites are the attempts. Chicago leads the NFL in time of possession margin, so Mayfield will have to make his possessions count, and the Bears allow big plays through the air, so I’d expect Mayfield to take some shots downfield. Pick: Baker Mayfield Over 29.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Bills (-3) at Vikings: O/U 43.5 Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings as Kyler Murray deals with an injured hamstring. Minnesota is coming off their first loss of the season, 19-15 to the Lions. Buffalo was off a bye for a hyped up game against Baltimore, but due to two quarterback injuries, the Bills ended up routing the Ravens 36-10 in a game Buffalo never trailed. Buffalo gets two backup quarterbacks back-to-back weeks as they go for their fourth-straight win. I like the chances that happen. Buffalo leads the NFL in points per drive (3.07), and Minnesota is first in points allowed per drive (1.18). The Bills have been involved in the highest-scoring games and the Vikings the fewest. It’s a clash of offense versus defense, but I think offense will win. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week Solak's plays | Walder's props Clay's TD projections Bowen's Game of the Week Indianapolis Colts at Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 44.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh Aaron Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three TDs last week, and Jaylen Warren had 126 total yards. Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images We need to have a bounce-back week here after betting on the Bills last Sunday. So, let's pivot to a rested Pittsburgh team that played Thursday night in Week 4 at home against an Indianapolis team straight off a London trip. We'll look at both sides of the ball, then hit some props from this game and across the league in Week 5. NFL betting • Best bets for Sunday: Cincy in danger? • Burrow passes Allen as MVP fave | Odds • Why Lawrence is the best MVP value • Betting favorites go 14-1 in Week 9 • Odds for Week 10 games | Early bets • Super Bowl odds: Jaguars move up • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Steelers have the ball: Running back Jaylen Warren has seen his usage (and production) elevate over the past two games. During this stretch (against Cincinnati and Cleveland) Warren has averaged 6.5 yards per carry, 21 touches and 151 scrimmage yards. He's also playing fast on the tape, and there's a lot of outside zone here, with Warren finding daylight. Plus, he's getting the ball on swings, screens and checkdowns. This is a good matchup for Warren against a Colts defense giving up 131 rushing yards per game (28th in the league). I expect a volume day for the Steelers' lead back. The Colts' defensive numbers in the pass game point to a Pittsburgh edge as well, as the Colts are giving up 261.3 yards per game through the air and are pressuring the QB at a rate of only 28.3% (29th in the league). But can the Steelers protect and give Aaron Rodgers time and a clean pocket? Rodgers has three touchdown passes and six completions of 15 or more air yards in each of his past two games, but he has been sacked seven times during that stretch and a total of 13 times on the season (tied for most in the league). Rodgers' declining mobility also plays a role, but he needs the pocket to throw vertically to DK Metcalf and work the play-action pass game in Mike McCarthy's offense. When the Colts have the ball: This offense runs through Jonathan Taylor . The Colts' running back ranks fifth in the NFL at 88.3 rushing yards per game, and his 86 carries are the third most through four games. He's a volume back with home run ability. Taylor has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season, and he gets a Steelers defense that is giving up 4.3 YPC (20th). I'd expect a run-heavy approach from the Colts to start this one, but the Steelers should counter with more single-high coverages, spinning down from their split-safety shells to get numbers in the front. Look for quarterback Daniel Jones to lean on play-action throws that mirror the run game. Jones ranks fifth in play-action attempts this season, and the Colts will look to open intermediate windows against a Steelers defense that plays heavy zone coverage (75.4% of coverage snaps). And without wide receiver Alec Pierce (IR/heel), there is a missing vertical element for the Colts, as Jones' 5.7 YPA ranks 28th. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen need to uncover and make themselves available to the QB in this one, and I would like to see tight end Tyler Warren featured more on seams and corner routes to create chunk plays. With the rushing totals and targets on screens and check downs, Taylor should hit the over. Jaylen Warren rushing yards OVER 62.5 (-112) Warren has rushed for at least 93 yards in two straight games, with 17 carries in each. Take Warren's recent run on production in a matchup versus a Colts defense allowing 4.8 YPC (sixth highest in the league). Now, let's get to some other bets I like ... Christian Watson anytime TD (+195) Watson has scored at least one touchdown in three of four games played, and he has four end zone targets on the season. Plus, we know Watson can separate over the top. I like the matchup here for the Packers' receiver against the Bears' cornerbacks, and Matt LaFleur can also scheme zone-beaters for Watson. San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks total points UNDER 45.5 (-105) In the two games these clubs played last season, the totals hit 30 and 16. Mike Macdonald has the scheme (and personnel) to limit the 49ers' offense. I'd take the under in this one. Three-team parlay (+638) Jacksonville Jaguars -7.5 vs. Philadelphia Eagles Cleveland Browns +1.5 at New York Jets Las Vegas Raiders +3.5 at New England Patriots The Jaguars might be the best team in football, and they get an Eagles squad that is going through major in-season transitions on the offensive line. Plus, Philly will be without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith . Cleveland also is playing good ball. Todd Monken's offense can take vertical shots in the pass game, and the downhill rushing attack is a foundational approach with Quinshon Judkins . The Browns can run the ball against a Jets defense that just gave up 232 yards on the ground to the Bears in Week 4. Let's finish this parlay with the Raiders getting points on the road in New England.
